In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The work done in stopping the car and the truck can be written as

W=Fx=∆KE

As both the car and the truck are moving initially with the same kinetic energy, after being stopped, they will have the same change of kinetic energy.

Also, they are stopped with the same applied force.

Hence, from the above equation, it can be written that they have the same displacement, i.e., x1=x2.

Acceleration is a vector quantity. As the direction of motion of the car is different in the two given situations, the acceleration of the car will not be the same.

questions.q: Which element is not present in Nessler’s reagent?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Nessler’s reagent, K2HgI4 is used to detect ammonia. It is a pale solution that gets darker yellow when some amount of ammonia is added. A brown precipitate may form at a higher concentration. Nessler's reagent can be crystallized from a concentrated solution of mercury iodide with potassium iodide.

So, the correct option is D.

questions.q:
Find the compound ' A ' from the following reaction sequences.
$\mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\text { aqua-regia }} \mathrm{B} \xrightarrow[\text { (2) } \mathrm{AcOH}]{\text { (1) } \mathrm{KNO}_2 \mid \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}} \text { yellow ppt }$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Compound $(A)$ in the given reaction sequence is likely to be CoS.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CoS}+\mathrm{HNO}_3+3 \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{Co}^{2+} & +\mathrm{S} \downarrow+\mathrm{NOCl} \uparrow \\ & +2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\end{aligned}$
The above solution is neutralised with $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$.
To a neutral solution of $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$, acetic acid and saturated solution of $\mathrm{KNO}_2$ are added which results in the formation of yellow precipitate of $\mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_6\right]\mathrm{Co}^{2+}+7 \mathrm{NO}_2^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}^{+}+3 \mathrm{~K}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_6\right]+\mathrm{NO} \uparrow+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

questions.q: The lanthanide ion that would show colour is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The elements or ions having unpaired electrons show colour. The valence shell electronic configuration of La3+ and Lu3+ are 4f0 and 4f14 respectively. Hence, they are colourless. Gd3+ is also colourless, this is because, here 4f orbitals are half filled,hence stable.As such f-f transitions are not possible because they will destroy the symmetry of 4f and make them unstable. Sm3+ has the valence shell electronic configuration 4f5, hence, it is coloured due to the presence of unpaired electrons.

La+3= Colourless
Gd+3= Colourless
Sm+3= Pale yellow colour
Lu+3= Colourless

questions.q:
For the following Assertion and Reason, the correct option is:
Assertion: For hydrogenation reactions, the catalytic activity increases from Group 5 to Group 11 metals with maximum activity shown by Group 7-9 elements.
Reason: The reactants are most strongly adsorbed on group 7-9 elements.
options: The assertion is true, but the reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false
Both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation for the assertion
Both assertion and reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation for the assertion
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: The general trend for the activity for hydrogenation increases from left to right. In Hydrogenation reaction, catalytic activity depends on variable oxidation states as well as atomic size. Hence for hydrogenation reactions, the catalytic activity increases from a group 5 to group 11 metals with maximum activity shown by group 7-9 elements.

questions.q:
A transition metal ' \(\mathrm{M}\) ' among \(\mathrm{Sc}, \mathrm{Ti}, \mathrm{V}, \mathrm{Cr}, \mathrm{Mn}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}\) has the highest second ionisation enthalpy. The spin-only magnetic moment value of \(\mathrm{M}^{+}\)ion is _______. \(\mathrm{BM}\) (Near integer)
(Given atomic number \(\mathrm{Sc}: 21, \mathrm{Ti}: 22, \mathrm{~V}: 23, \mathrm{Cr}: 24, \mathrm{Mn}: 25, \mathrm{Fe}: 26\))
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Among given metals, $\mathrm{Cr}$ has maximum $\mathrm{IE}_2$
because Second electron is removed from stable configuration $3 d^5\mathrm{Cr}^{+}:[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^5 4 \mathrm{~s}^0\therefore$ No of unpaired $\mathrm{e}^{-}$in $\mathrm{Cr}^{+}$is $5, \mathrm{n}=5\begin{aligned}
\text { So, Magnetic moment } & =\sqrt{\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{n}+2)} \text { B.M } \\
& =\sqrt{5(5+2)}=5.92 \quad \mathrm{BM} \approx 6
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The number of electrons involved in the reduction of permanganate to manganese dioxide in acidic medium is _____ .
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Permanganate is reduced to Manganese dioxide by the following reaction:
MnO4-+7+4H++3e-⟶Mn+4O2+2H2O
Here, oxidation no. of manganese was reduced by 3 from reactant to product side. Thus, three electrons are involved.

questions.q: An acidified manganate solution undergoes disproportionation reaction. The spin-only magnetic moment value of the product having manganese in higher oxidation state is____B.M. (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
3MnO42-+4H+⟶2MnO4-+MnO2+2H2O

As we can see in this reaction oxidised product of reaction is MnO4- which has no unpaired electrons. So, magnetic moment will be zero.

Mn= no. of unpaired electrons is '0'
